title: SoMa: Identifying, Exploring, and Understanding the DRAM Communication Scheduling Space for DNN Accelerators
problem: As on-chip buffers on DNN accelerators grow large enough to hold most single-layer weights, single-layer dataflow optimization no longer meaningfully reduces DRAM bandwidth pressure. Multi-layer fusion and DRAM communication scheduling (timing of prefetches and stores across fused layers) remain an open, poorly-characterized optimization problem.
motivation: DRAM bandwidth is a persistent bottleneck for DNN accelerators; with larger SRAMs enabling multi-layer fusion, the opportunity to reduce DRAM traffic through cross-layer prefetch/store scheduling is large but the search space is not well understood.
method: SoMa introduces Tensor-centric Notation (TCN), a formal system that describes all possible ways to schedule when data is fetched from and stored to main memory (DRAM) during execution of multiple fused neural network layers. A scheduling compiler uses this notation to explore trade-offs in when to prefetch data, when to store results, and how to group layers together, optimizing for different accelerators and workloads. The framework has been deployed as a compiler in a commercial accelerator product.
key_novelty: SoMa's Tensor-centric Notation formally defines all possible DRAM data-scheduling strategies when executing multiple fused neural network layers together, enabling a compiler to jointly optimize them instead of tuning each layer separately.
contributions: Identification of DRAM communication scheduling (multi-layer prefetch/store timing) as the key untapped optimization dimension beyond single-layer dataflow.
Tensor-centric Notation (TCN) and parsing method to represent and explore the full DRAM communication scheduling space.
End-to-end SoMa scheduling compiler achieving 2.11x performance improvement and 37.3% energy reduction vs. state-of-the-art Cocco framework.
LLM scheduling analysis and design space exploration (DSE) using SoMa; open-sourced at GitHub.
limitations: The framework's effectiveness on irregular/dynamic-shape workloads (e.g., LLM autoregressive decode with variable sequence length) is not thoroughly evaluated.
primary_theme: Compiler-driven DRAM communication scheduling across fused DNN layers
